scenes.text: You've spent years arguing about offside, with four rules that don't exist.
Myth one: he was level, so he's offside. False. Level with the second-last opponent is onside.
Myth two: his arm was past the defender. Still no. Hands and arms never count: only head, body and feet.
Myth three: he was all alone when he got the ball. So what? The snapshot is taken when his team-mate plays the ball, not when it arrives.
Myth four: standing in an offside position is already an offence. No. Position alone is never punished: he has to get involved in play.
And a bonus: if the ball comes to you straight from a throw-in, a goal kick or a corner, there's no offside.
Offside isn't just where you are. It's when, with what, and what you do.
Save it, and share it with the friend who calls everything offside from the sofa.
